point: noun
an idea or fact that someone makes in a discussion
typical: make/see/take a point, a good point. NOT for: sharp end or score.
That's a good point.
I see your point.
noun
the main idea or most important fact
typical: the point is..., get/miss the point. NOT for: purpose.
The point is that we have no time.
You're missing the point.
noun
the purpose or use of something
typical: no point in + -ing, what's the point of...? NOT for: ideas in a debate.
There's no point in waiting.
What's the point of this rule?
noun
a particular moment or stage in time or in a process
typical: at this point, at some point, up to a point. NOT for: places on a map.
At this point, we had no choice.
I'll call you at some point tomorrow.
noun
a unit of score in a game or test
typical: score/win/lose a point. NOT for: ideas.
She scored ten points in the game.
We lost by two points.
verb
show direction or draw attention using your finger
typical: point at/to/towards + thing. NOT for: ideas or purpose.
He pointed at the door.
Point to the correct picture.
play: verb
take part in a game or sport
typical: play + football/chess/cards, play for + team. NOT for: music.
They play football on Sundays.
Do you play chess?
verb
make music with an instrument, or make a recording or device produce sound
typical: play the piano/guitar, play a song/CD. NOT for: games.
She plays the piano.
Play that song again.
verb
perform a part in a film, play or show
typical: play a role/part/character. NOT for: sports.
He plays the main character in the film.
She played Juliet at school.
verb
(of children) do things for fun
typical: children play in the garden/with toys. NOT for: organized sports.
The children are playing in the garden.
The kids play with their toys.
verb
have an effect or role in something
typical: play a part/role in sth, play an important role. NOT for: acting.
Education plays an important role in society.
Luck played a big part in his success.
noun
a story written to be performed by actors in a theatre
typical: a play by Shakespeare, go to a play. NOT for: games.
We saw a play by Chekhov.
The school play is next week.
noun
activity done for fun, especially by children
typical: children's play, at play. NOT for: theatre.
Play is important to a child's development.
The children were at play in the yard.
put: verb
move something to a place or position
typical: put + object + on/in/at + place. NOT for: phrasal meanings like put off, put up.
Put the bag on the table.
She put the milk in the fridge.
verb
cause someone or something to be in a state or situation
typical: put sb in a good mood/danger, put sth in order. NOT for: placing objects.
The news put me in a bad mood.
Don't put yourself in danger.
verb
write or print something somewhere
typical: put your name on a list, put it in writing. NOT for: speaking.
Put your name at the top of the page.
Please put your signature here.
verb
express something in words
typical: put it simply/mildly/another way. NOT for: placing objects.
Let me put it simply.
How would you put that in English?
verb
suggest or ask something formally
typical: put a question/proposal/idea to sb. NOT for: placing objects.
She put a question to the speaker.
They put a proposal to the board.
verb
consider something to have a particular value or importance
typical: put sth above/before sth, put emphasis on sth. NOT for: physical placing.
He puts his family before his career.
The company puts great emphasis on safety.
